note: The website itself is finished. Everything left is either moving it to its permanent home, or filling in work that only the family can supply — photographs, and two decisions about what to say about Venuka. Items marked 'on hold' are not counted in the progress figure; they are things worth doing one day, not things holding anything up.

phases.title: Move to its permanent home
phases.dates: decided 3–4 Nov 2026 · not yet carried out

phases.title: Fill in the collection
phases.dates: ongoing, as new work is made

tasks.title: Decide where the site should live
tasks.doneWhen: The address and the host are settled, and the reasoning is written down where it can be checked later.

subs.t: Weigh a subdomain against buying a domain
subs.n: Hara asked, 3 Nov 2026. Settled on artbyvenuka.nischayacreativesoft.com — free, and the company domain was already in hand.

subs.t: Check what the company domain is actually doing today
subs.n: Read live on 3 Nov: GitHub's four addresses on the bare domain, www pointing at the same account, one Google verification line, no email records, no other subdomains. The new subdomain sits beside all of it and disturbs none of it.

subs.t: Settle whether the repository should be private
subs.n: Decided private on 4 Nov, then reopened on 6 Nov. Three decisions had been bundled into one — the host, the privacy and the address — and only the privacy one forces a change of host. The address is available on all three routes, so it is not what is being decided. Still open.

subs.t: Confirm what a private repository costs on GitHub
subs.n: Checked against GitHub's own documentation, 4 Nov: free accounts can publish a website only from a public repository. Hence the move to Cloudflare.

subs.t: Confirm Cloudflare can serve a subdomain without moving the domain
subs.n: Checked against Cloudflare's own documentation, 4 Nov: a subdomain needs only one record at GoDaddy. The nameservers stay where they are.

subs.t: Write the decision and the steps down
subs.n: DEPLOYMENT.md rewritten end to end, 4 Nov, and committed.

subs.t: Lay the three ways out side by side
subs.n: Added to the Diagrams tab on 6 Nov, with what each one costs and what each one leaves readable, so the choice can be looked at rather than argued from memory.

subs.t: Check what a paid GitHub plan actually costs
subs.n: The third route — private repository, stay on GitHub Pages, no Cloudflare. Worth a look before ruling it out on price.

tasks.title: Keep the working notes off the website
tasks.doneWhen: The published site contains the eleven pages and nothing else, and that is true automatically rather than by anyone remembering.

subs.t: Write something that copies only the website
subs.n: Done 4 Nov. It works from a list of what belongs, so anything new is left out by default rather than needing to be noticed.

subs.t: Prove it by actually serving the result
subs.n: Served it and asked for each document by name: all of them returned 'not found'. The site itself rendered correctly with no errors.

subs.t: Make it part of the real publishing step
subs.n: Put into the GitHub workflow on 4 Nov and verified on the live site: every working document returns not-found. It goes in again as the Cloudflare build command when that is connected.

tasks.title: Make the repository private
tasks.doneWhen: The code and notes are private, and no half-switched-off publishing is left behind.

subs.t: Switch the repository to private
Switch GitHub Pages off
subs.n: Otherwise a stale public copy is left sitting there.

subs.t: Remove the old publishing step
subs.n: Deleted 4 Nov. It had just published three working files to the public web because its list of what to leave out was out of date. Fixed to use the assembler, checked that every document returned not-found, then removed so nothing can publish until Cloudflare is connected. The live site is frozen where it is.

subs.t: Tell anyone who has the old link
subs.n: The current github.io address stops working the moment the repository goes private.

tasks.title: Connect Cloudflare Pages
tasks.doneWhen: A change pushed from the computer appears on Cloudflare's own free address a minute later, with the checks having run first.

subs.t: Make a Cloudflare account
Connect it to the repository, that one only
subs.n: Choose 'only select repositories' rather than all of them, so Cloudflare can read this project and nothing else.

subs.t: Set the build command and the output folder
subs.n: The checks and the assembler as the command; the assembled folder as the output.

subs.t: Deploy once and open the free address

tasks.title: Point the subdomain at it
tasks.doneWhen: artbyvenuka.nischayacreativesoft.com loads the site over a secure connection, and the company site is unchanged.

subs.t: Add the domain in Cloudflare first
subs.n: Order matters. Creating the record at GoDaddy before Cloudflare knows about the domain gives visitors an error until it settles.

subs.t: Add the one record at GoDaddy
subs.n: A CNAME on 'artbyvenuka'. The bare domain and www records are the company site and must not be touched.

subs.t: Wait for the secure certificate
subs.n: Usually minutes. Cloudflare shows 'Active' when it is ready.

subs.t: Check the company site still loads

tasks.title: Tell the site its new address
tasks.doneWhen: Pasting the link into WhatsApp shows Venuka's frog-and-duck drawing.

subs.t: Run the address setter
subs.n: Best left until the subdomain actually answers, so the site does not spend days pointing at an address that is not there yet.

subs.t: Run the checks and publish
Paste the link into WhatsApp and look

tasks.title: Check it over after the move
tasks.doneWhen: Every item on the list in the publishing guide passes on the real address.

subs.t: The scene moves and the butterflies fly
Search, filters and full-size view all work
A video plays
Open it on a phone
A wrong address shows the friendly page
Asking for a working document returns 'not found'
subs.n: The one that matters most. If this fails, the notes are on the web.

tasks.title: Photograph the crafts
tasks.doneWhen: At least one craft photograph is on the site and the empty state is gone.

subs.t: Photograph a finished craft
subs.n: Waiting on the family. The page, the card and the folder are all ready and have been since 30 August.

subs.t: Add it to the content file
subs.n: One short entry; the guide explains each field.

tasks.title: Re-count the videos on the channel
tasks.doneWhen: The number of videos on the channel but not on the site is known again, and each one is either added or deliberately left out.

subs.t: Compare the channel against the site
subs.n: Last counted 30 August: seven missing. The collection has grown from 14 drawings to 23 since, so that number is stale.

subs.t: Add the ones worth adding
Decide about a daily automatic check
subs.n: Would remove the counting by hand, but it is machinery to maintain for a site that gains a video every few weeks.

tasks.title: Fill the gaps in the drawing entries
tasks.doneWhen: Every drawing has a date, and materials where they are known.

subs.t: Four drawings have no date
subs.n: Starry Night with Moon, Rainbow by the Lake, Pink Flowers on Blue, Colourful Landscape Layers. They sort to the end of 'newest first' until dated.

subs.t: Nine drawings have no materials listed
subs.n: They show 'Not recorded yet' rather than a guess — honest, but a real answer is better.

subs.t: Photograph the 13 drawings that only have a video still
subs.n: They look fine as they are. Worth doing slowly, a few at a time, not as a job.

tasks.title: The photograph of Venuka
tasks.doneWhen: The family has decided either way, and the About page reflects it.

subs.t: Decide whether to publish it
subs.n: Open since 30 August. A private repository does not change this — the website is public either way.

subs.t: Add it, if the answer is yes
subs.n: The space is already on the page.

tasks.title: Her school year and board
tasks.doneWhen: A decision is made, rather than it staying off the page by default.

subs.t: Decide whether they go back on the About page
subs.n: On the old Google Site; left out here because it identifies a child alongside her first name and her drawings.

tasks.title: Count the visitors
tasks.doneWhen: The page shows how many people visit, without cookies and without a consent banner.

subs.t: Add the Cloudflare analytics key
subs.n: One line in the content file. You will be in the Cloudflare dashboard anyway for the hosting move, so it costs about a minute then.

tasks.title: Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp
tasks.doneWhen: Either the links are published, or the slots are removed for good.

subs.t: Decide whether the site should have them at all
subs.n: The slots exist and say plainly that nothing is published yet. For a child's site, the YouTube channel and the form may be enough.
